findings.message: Instance fix of the round-3 get_release finding. The incomplete-ref check runs inside `isRelease`, and `isRelease` only runs as the `find` predicate on each row. If `listReleases(v)` returns no rows, `releaseWhere` never runs, so the call returns `null` ('not found') instead of the 'say which release' refusal. Whether a malformed call gets refused now depends on the data, so `get_release` and `get_release_history` still disagree. The new table test passes only because the fixtures give sahan visible releases. Fix: check the ref before the read (`releaseWhere(a)` at the top of `run`, or a zod `.refine` on `releaseRef`). Add a test case where the viewer can see no releases.
findings.scenario: A tenant or data scope with no releases calls get_release {} or { projectKey: 'CON' } → null ('release not found'). get_release_history with the same arguments throws 'say which release'.

findings.message: The repin is applied only to this tab's React `pins` state. The architecture says a conversation's pins are persisted in `chat.conversation`, and `confirmChat`/`repinOf` never rewrite the stored pins. Three cases keep the stale `{ projectKey, version: old }` or `{ projectKey, name: old }` args: reopening the conversation from History, another tab with the same conversation open, and any other conversation that pinned the same release or environment. Fix: apply `repinAll` to the stored pins on the server inside the confirm path, then return the updated pins to the client.
findings.scenario: Pin 'Contoso Portal v2.4.0' (get_release { projectKey: 'CON', version: 'v2.4.0' }), confirm a re-tag to v2.4.1, close the drawer, reopen the conversation from Chat history and ask about the pin → get_release returns null.

findings.message: The label is rewritten by replacing every substring match (`split(old).join(new)`), so a short old name also changes unrelated parts of the label, such as the project key or project name. Replace only the label part built from the old name, for example the last whole-word match or a rebuilt label.
findings.scenario: Renaming environment 'A' to 'B' in project CAA turns the pin label 'CAA A' into 'CBB B'.

findings.message: The docblock 'One release with its proposals and full deployment history…' is now stranded above `ReleaseRef`/`releaseWhere`, so `getRelease` has lost its doc comment and `ReleaseRef` has two. Move it back above `getRelease`.

When an id is given, the lookups now treat the narrowing project key differently. get_environment and get_deployment return null when the id belongs to another project. get_release and get_release_history (releaseWhere/isRelease) ignore projectKey/version when releaseId is set. Pick one rule for every ref read.
findings.scenario: get_release_history({ releaseId: <CON release>, projectKey: 'HRI' }) returns the CON release, while get_environment({ environmentId: <CON env>, projectKey: 'HRI' }) returns null.
